From 874f224cc52d64c912087e68e3724be95ad80ee7 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Stephen Boyd <sboyd@codeaurora.org>
Date: Fri, 18 Apr 2014 16:29:43 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] clk: Fix slab corruption in clk_unregister()

When a clock is unregsitered, we iterate over the list of
children and reparent them to NULL (i.e. orphan list). While
iterating the list, we should use the safe iterators because the
children list for this clock is changing when we reparent the
children to NULL. Failure to iterate safely can lead to slab
corruption like this:

=============================================================================
BUG kmalloc-128 (Not tainted): Poison overwritten

diff --git a/drivers/clk/clk.c b/drivers/clk/clk.c
index f71093bf83ab..7cf2c093cc54 100644
--- a/drivers/clk/clk.c
+++ b/drivers/clk/clk.c
@@ -2140,9 +2140,10 @@ void clk_unregister(struct clk *clk)
 
 	if (!hlist_empty(&clk->children)) {
 		struct clk *child;
+		struct hlist_node *t;
 
 		/* Reparent all children to the orphan list. */
-		hlist_for_each_entry(child, &clk->children, child_node)
+		hlist_for_each_entry_safe(child, t, &clk->children, child_node)
 			clk_set_parent(child, NULL);
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/clk/clk.c`**
   - The patch modifies the `clk_unregister` function.
   - The iteration over the list of children clocks has been changed from `hlist_for_each_entry` to `hlist_for_each_entry_safe`. 
   - A new variable `struct hlist_node *t;` has been introduced to safely store the next node in the list during iteration.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The change from `hlist_for_each_entry` to `hlist_for_each_entry_safe` is crucial because it allows for safe iteration over the list while modifying it (reparenting the children to NULL). This prevents potential slab corruption that could occur if the list is altered during iteration, ensuring the integrity of memory management in the clock subsystem.

The bug occurs due to unsafe iteration over the list of children clocks in the `clk_unregister` function. When a clock is unregistered, the function attempts to reparent its children to NULL while iterating through the list. This modification of the list during iteration can lead to slab corruption, as the iterator may access invalid memory locations after the list has been altered.

Here is the patch:
  */
 void clk_unregister(struct clk *clk)
 {
 	unsigned long flags;
 
        if (!clk || WARN_ON_ONCE(IS_ERR(clk)))
                return;
 
 	clk_prepare_lock();
 
 	if (clk->ops == &clk_nodrv_ops) {
 		pr_err("%s: unregistered clock: %s\n", __func__, clk->name);
 		goto out;
 	}
 	/*
 	 * Assign empty clock ops for consumers that might still hold
 	 * a reference to this clock.
 	 */
 	flags = clk_enable_lock();
 	clk->ops = &clk_nodrv_ops;
 	clk_enable_unlock(flags);
 
 	if (!hlist_empty(&clk->children)) {
 		struct clk *child;
+		struct hlist_node *t;
 
 		/* Reparent all children to the orphan list. */
-		hlist_for_each_entry(child, &clk->children, child_node)
+		hlist_for_each_entry_safe(child, t, &clk->children, child_node)
 			clk_set_parent(child, NULL);
 	}
 
 	clk_debug_unregister(clk);
 
 	hlist_del_init(&clk->child_node);
 
 	if (clk->prepare_count)
 		pr_warn("%s: unregistering prepared clock: %s\n",
 					__func__, clk->name);
 
 	kref_put(&clk->ref, __clk_release);
 out:
 	clk_prepare_unlock();
 }
 EXPORT_SYMBOL_GPL(clk_unregister);

struct hlist_node *t;
